sentences.text: Megaraptor was a robust carnivorous theropod measuring between 8 and 9 meters in length.
Estimates suggest the animal reached a mass of one tonne.
Its skull was relatively gracile and weak compared to other theropods, likely because its powerful and mobile forelimbs reduced the need for a strong skull during predation.
The neck consisted of ten cervical vertebrae.
The name Megaraptor namunhuaiquii means "giant thief with a spear in the foot" in Greek and Mapudungun.
Megaraptor was initially thought to be a giant dromaeosaurid, later classified as an allosauroid, and most recently placed as a basal tyrannosauroid.
The large first finger phalanx had a wide dorsal surface and sharp inner edge strong enough to support a massive extensor muscle.
The strong hyperextension of the claw suggests it was adapted for raptorial habits.
The genus Megaraptor was described by Fernando E. Novas in 1998.
Fernando E. Novas recovered the fragmentary remains of Megaraptor in January 1996.
Fossils of Megaraptor were found in the Portezuelo Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.
Megaraptor was described in 1998 by Fernando Novas, initially as a large carnivore likely belonging to the dromaeosaurid family.
Due to its gracile skull, Megaraptor likely relied on large hand claws to grab prey items and pull them toward its chest.
Researchers suggest Megaraptor may have had mobile forelimbs adapted to grip prey and draw it toward the jaws for dispatching.
While it was initially suggested that Megaraptor used its hand claws to open carcasses, active predation is now generally favored.
Researchers suggested Megaraptor may have been social, comparing it to lions and hyenas based on specimens found in close proximity.
It was later suggested that specimens found in close proximity may have accumulated post-mortem rather than indicating social behavior.
Researchers noted that the presence of tympanic sinuses suggests Megaraptor's actual hearing range was lower than calculated from cochlear duct length.
Evidence regarding Megaraptor's diet is weak because only hand morphology is available for comparison, lacking cranial materials.
Megaraptor's hand morphology is comparable to that of the basal tetanuran Baryonyx.
Megaraptor namunhuaiquii is classified within the infraorder Coelurosauria.
In 2012, researchers erected the clade Megaraptora to include Megaraptor namunhuaiquii and its closest relatives.
In 2004, it was suggested that Megaraptor belonged to a novel lineage predating the split between carnosaurs and coelurosaurs.
It is debated whether Megaraptor belongs to the allosaurids, carcarodontosaurids, megalosaurids, or represents a distinct group entirely.
Calvo and colleagues suggested Megaraptor was a basal tetanuran rather than a coelurosaur.
Megaraptor fossils date to the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Turonian and Coniacian ages.
Megaraptor lived approximately 90 to 88 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
Megaraptor lived during the middle to late Cretaceous, approximately 98 million years ago, between the Turonian and Coniacian stages.
Megaraptor fossils are known from the Late Turonian to Early Coniacian Portezuelo Formation in Argentina.
Megaraptor lived in a fluvial environment with a humid climate.
Megaraptor shared its ecosystem with Elemgasem, Futalogknosaurus, Unenlagia, and Argentinadraco.
A 2025 paper noted morphological inconsistencies between the juvenile specimen and larger specimens referred to M. namunhuaiquii.

In 2025, researchers used allometry to suggest that a fully mature Megaraptor skull would likely have been deeper, more robust, and had proportionally smaller eye sockets than the known juvenile specimen.
